context_heading: Understanding independence and charges when comparing IFAs
context: Independent financial advisers must justify their independent status, meaning they consider products from across the market rather than a limited panel. When comparing, ask each adviser to explain whether their advice is independent or restricted, and how they charge, so you can weigh up the difference.

Charges should be discussed in pounds, not just percentages, so you can compare the actual cost of advice between firms. You can also ask about qualifications such as Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute or the Personal Finance Society, and certifications like CFP, which show advanced training.

faqs.q: How can I compare independent financial advisers near me?
faqs.a: Start by checking each adviser's status on the FCA register and asking whether their advice is independent or restricted. Then compare their charges in pounds and their qualifications, such as Chartered status or CFP certification, so you can judge which one suits your needs.

faqs.q: What does 'best' mean when comparing IFAs?
faqs.a: There is no single 'best' adviser, as it depends on your circumstances and what you need advice on. Focus on independence, clear charges in pounds, relevant qualifications and how well they explain things, then decide what matters most to you.

faqs.q: Is iComply regulated and does it give financial advice?
faqs.a: No, iComply is not regulated and does not provide financial advice. We are an introduction service that connects you with a suitable UK financial adviser, who will quote you directly and give any advice.

faqs.q: What should I have ready when I speak to an adviser?
faqs.a: Have an idea of your goals, any existing pensions or investments, and your budget for advice. The adviser will ask about your circumstances to compare products across the market if they are independent.

extra_heading: Making a fair comparison when you search for the best
extra: The word 'best' in your search is personal: the best adviser for you depends on what you need advice on, such as a pension review or a new investment, and how you prefer to work with someone. Rather than looking for an overall winner, compare local independent financial advisers on the things that matter to you, like how clearly they explain their charges in pounds and whether their qualifications suit your situation.

A genuinely independent adviser must justify their independent status by considering products from across the market, so ask each one you compare to explain how they do this and whether their advice is independent or restricted. You can also check that every adviser or firm you are considering is authorised on the FCA register, and ask about advanced qualifications such as Chartered status or CFP certification.

When you speak to an adviser, you can ask how they would approach your specific need and what information they would need from you, so you can compare their answers side by side. Remember that iComply does not give advice or compare advisers for you; we simply introduce you to a suitable UK financial adviser who will quote you directly, and you decide who to proceed with.
